claims.text: The relevant nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and are initially crystallized as a solid solution.
Maintenance of structural and chemical stability from 473 to 1923 K is governed by the solid solution's ability to resist phase separation and chemical ordering.
High-temperature in situ X-ray diffraction or spectroscopy can monitor phase changes and chemical composition.
Phase separation and chemical ordering are the structural mediators of stability loss.
Real-time observation by high-temperature in situ X-ray diffraction or spectroscopy is the proposed mechanism.
Nanoparticles that retain a solid-solution structure and resist phase separation and chemical ordering will exhibit improved structural and chemical stability over the operating range.
Particle size and shape may affect nanoparticle stability.
Significant phase separation or chemical ordering below 1923 K would indicate loss of structural and chemical stability.

contradictions.description: The mechanism is stated as an observational measurement method rather than a physical process connecting phase separation or ordering to stability.
